title: Porter Welfare on Kilimanjaro: What Fair Treatment Looks Like
excerpt: Porters make every Kilimanjaro climb possible. This is what fair treatment looks like, and which questions to ask your operator.
body:
Porters are the backbone of every Kilimanjaro climb. Unfortunately, not every operator treats them well. As a climber, you can make a difference by choosing carefully.

## What fair treatment means

- **Fair pay**, paid in full and on time, separate from tips.
- **Reasonable loads.** The park sets a maximum weight per porter; good operators weigh bags at the gate.
- **Proper clothing and gear**: warm jackets, boots, sleeping bags and a tent to sleep in.
- **Good food**, three meals a day.
- **Medical care** and evacuation if a porter gets sick or injured.
- **Fair tipping**, where tips reach the crew directly.

## The Kilimanjaro Porters Assistance Project

The Kilimanjaro Porters Assistance Project (KPAP) is an organisation that monitors porter treatment and works with partner companies. Operators can be part of its partner programme. Ask an operator whether they work with KPAP or a similar initiative.

## Questions to ask your operator

1. What do porters earn per day?
2. How do you check porter loads?
3. Where do porters sleep and what do they eat?
4. What equipment do porters receive?
5. How are tips distributed?

## Red flags

Very low prices are often a sign that someone in the chain is paid too little. Park fees are fixed, so savings usually come from the crew.

## Our approach

We work with Kilimanjaro Nature Tours, our partner in Arusha. Ask us any of the questions above; we will answer openly. Read more about [responsible tourism](/responsible-tourism-tanzania/) and [plan your climb](/travel-proposal/).
